In [[algebraic geometry]], a [[Morphism of schemes|morphism]] <math>f: X \to Y</math> between [[scheme (algebraic geometry)|scheme]]s is said to be '''quasi-compact''' if ''Y'' can be covered by [[open set|open]] [[affine scheme|affine]] subschemes <math>V_i</math> such that the pre-images <math>f^{-1}(V_i)</math> are [[compact space|compact]].<ref>This is the definition in Hartshorne.</ref> If ''f'' is quasi-compact, then the pre-image of a compact open subscheme (e.g., open affine subscheme) under ''f'' is compact.

It is not enough that ''Y'' admits a covering by compact open subschemes whose pre-images are compact. To give an example,<ref>Remark 1.5 in Vistoli</ref>  let ''A'' be a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]] that does not satisfy the [[ascending chain condition]]s on [[radical ideal]]s, and put <math>X = \operatorname{Spec} A</math>. Then ''X'' contains an open subset ''U'' that is not compact. Let ''Y'' be the scheme obtained by [[Gluing schemes | gluing]] two ''X'''s along ''U''. ''X'', ''Y'' are both compact. If <math>f: X \to Y</math> is the inclusion of one of the copies of ''X'', then the pre-image of the other ''X'', open affine in ''Y'', is ''U''—not compact. Hence, ''f'' is not quasi-compact.

A morphism from a quasi-compact scheme to an affine scheme is quasi-compact.

Let <math>f: X \to Y</math> be a quasi-compact morphism between schemes. Then <math>f(X)</math> is closed if and only if it is stable under specialization.

The composition of quasi-compact morphisms is quasi-compact. The base change of a quasi-compact morphism is quasi-compact.

{{expert needed|Mathematics |talk=Quasi-compact schemes vs. quasi-compact morphisms|date=August 2023}}

An affine scheme is quasi-compact. In fact, a scheme is quasi-compact if and only if it is a finite union of open affine subschemes. [[Serre's theorem on affineness|Serre's criterion]] gives a necessary and sufficient condition for a quasi-compact scheme to be affine.

A quasi-compact scheme has at least one [[closed point]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Schwede | first = Karl
 | contribution = Gluing schemes and a scheme without closed points
 | doi = 10.1090/conm/386/07222
 | mr = 2182775
 | pages = 157–172
 | publisher = Amer. Math. Soc., Providence, RI
 | series = Contemp. Math.
 | title = Recent progress in arithmetic and algebraic geometry
 | volume = 386
 | year = 2005| isbn = 978-0-8218-3401-5
 }}. See in particular Proposition&nbsp;4.1.</ref>
